scores.reason: In an adult with hyperinsulinaemic hypoglycaemia, very high total insulin plus insulin autoantibodies and PEG precipitation determine the diagnosis of insulin autoimmune syndrome and steer away from imaging or surgery; C-peptide separates exogenous insulin. Other tests (antibody assay alone) can partly substitute, so 3 not 4.

scores.reason: Ordered by an endocrinologist during a hypoglycaemia work-up; insulin antibodies and PEG precipitation are send-out or special-lab steps (score 1 if the protocol is read as complex). Chose 2 for specialist outpatient ownership.

Test burden 3 (blood draw, ideally during a spontaneous low glucose). False-result consequence 2: a missed or misread result leads to repeat imaging or an unnecessary pancreatic procedure, which is reversible only if caught early. Lower of the two is 2.

Without the measurement the default is an insulinoma work-up with imaging and possible surgery while hypoglycaemia continues; the harm is serious (hospitalisation, unnecessary pancreatic surgery) but the syndrome is usually self-limited once the trigger is stopped. Alternative reading is 2.

Prior gestational diabetes: the project found no insulin or HOMA test used; testing relies on OGTT or A1C and metformin is offered on ADA criteria (Rec 3.7) without an insulin result. A fasting-insulin or HOMA result would change nothing beyond what is in hand.
sources: ADA Standards of Care 2026 section 3, first 100k of 159k characters read (usecases-verified.md row 45)

scores.reason: Fasting insulin (measure type: fasting-based) would be ordered by primary care or obstetric follow-up as a routine laboratory test with one fasting draw; no clinical pathway uses the result.
Test burden 3 or 4 (one fasting draw). False-result consequence 3: false reassurance or overdiagnosis could delay or add metformin, but the OGTT/A1C screen continues regardless. Lower is 3.

Marginal harm of not measuring insulin is minor because the default (OGTT/A1C screening, metformin or lifestyle prevention per ADA) already covers the patient. Score would be 1 if insulin were shown to find progressors that glucose misses.
C-peptide as one input to a remission score (ABCD or Diabetes Surgery Score) is used for pre-operative counselling, not for eligibility; per clarification 11 prognosis that sets counselling is 1.
sources: PMID 22963817 abstract (DOI not recorded in usecases-verified.md)

scores.reason: Ordered by bariatric surgery or endocrine clinic at pre-operative evaluation; a single random or fasting C-peptide is a routine laboratory add-on, but the score is used by the specialist team.
Test burden 3 (blood draw; unreliable on insulin therapy or CKD). False-result consequence 2: wrong remission expectations or a patient discouraged from surgery. Lower is 2.
sources: usecases-verified.md row 11 (unreliable with insulin therapy or CKD; cutoff study-specific)

scores.reason: Surgery proceeds on other grounds; without C-peptide the patient has less precise counselling on remission odds (duration of diabetes alone performs similarly at 10 years). Symptomatic and reversible at most.

Stimulated C-peptide (post-load or mixed-meal) as a trial endpoint tells investigators whether an intervention preserved beta-cell function; for an individual patient in routine care it changes nothing, at most counselling about honeymoon or residual function. Anchor does not fit research endpoints well, see anchor_issues.
A 2-hour or 4-hour mixed-meal tolerance test with timed draws run by a specialist or research unit; no routine owner outside trials.
Test burden 2 (2 to 4 hour visit, repeated draws, hyperglycaemia and renal clearance limit interpretation). False-result consequence 3 (research conclusions, not patient care). Lower is 2.
Not measuring C-peptide in routine care causes no patient harm; the research use affects trial interpretation, not an individual's outcome. The regulatory eligibility use is row 29, not scored here.

In an infant with high measured insulin, PEG precipitation of maternal and infant samples decides whether the value is real or an assay artefact from antibodies, so it determines the diagnosis (congenital hyperinsulinism or not); glucose response, ketones and genetics could partly substitute.
sources: PMID 42697708 abstract (Ismail and Wilkinson-Herbots 2026; DOI not recorded in usecases-verified.md)

scores.reason: Paediatric endocrinology with a specialised laboratory step (PEG precipitation, maternal sample); few sites run it. Specialist-only with a complex protocol.

Test burden 2 (infant blood draw, maternal sample). False-result consequence 1: a misread result leads to a congenital hyperinsulinism label with diazoxide or further imaging, or the reverse, a missed real case in an infant.

Without the interpretation the default is to treat as congenital hyperinsulinism (diazoxide, extended work-up); moderate, mostly reversible harm. A reading with surgery in the default pathway would be 3.

MMTT C-peptide (mixed-meal) before total pancreatectomy with islet autotransplant counsels on expected insulin need; the operation is chosen on pain and pancreatitis grounds. No preoperative threshold was found, and in the distal pancreatectomy cohort preoperative C-peptide AUC was not significant (PMID 37889837).
sources: PMID 37889837 DOI 10.1210/clinem/dgad634 abstract and full-text windows (as recorded in usecases-verified.md)

scores.reason: Ordered by the pancreas surgery or islet transplant programme; MMTT requires a timed protocol in a specialist unit, but the programme owns it as part of the evaluation.
Test burden 2 (2 to 4 hour MMTT in a patient who may have pancreatic disease). False-result consequence 2: wrong insulin-need counselling; the decision to operate does not rest on it. Lower is 2.
Operation proceeds and glucose is monitored after it regardless; without the pre-operative value the harm is less accurate counselling and possibly later recognition of insulin need.

Adult with suspected reactive hypoglycaemia: the diagnosis rests on symptoms with a documented low glucose (post-load or mixed-meal); insulin was collected but not used as a criterion in either study, and no threshold was found. The insulin part adds counselling at most. The glucose part of the same test would be 2.

scores.reason: A 5-hour OGTT or MMTT is ordered by endocrinology or by primary care referral; timed protocol, no routine pathway. Specialist outpatient.

Test burden 2 (5-hour visit, symptoms may be provoked). False-result consequence 2: 30% of 40 symptomatic adults met a low-glucose cut-off the authors set themselves, so overdiagnosis and unnecessary dietary restriction are plausible. Lower is 2.
sources: PMID 33916952 abstract and full-text windows (as recorded)

scores.reason: Symptomatic but reversible; the default (dietary advice, reassurance) is low risk, and a missed insulinoma is covered by row 23, not this situation.

anchor_issues: Row 8, D1: the anchors score patient decisions; a research endpoint has no patient decision. Chose 1 (counselling at most) and noted that a trial-eligibility reading would score higher.

Row 20 and 25, D5: specialist outpatient (2) conflicts with specialist-only with a complex protocol (1) when the test is a send-out step. Chose 2 for the adult endocrine work-up (row 20) and 1 for the paediatric PEG step (row 25).
Row 48, D1: the test is glucose plus insulin; scored the insulin measurement only (1), because the diagnosis rests on glucose. Scoring the whole test would give 2.
Rows 11 and 27, D1: prognosis for counselling (1) versus selecting a diagnostic step (2); chose 1 because neither result gates the operation.
assumptions: No new searches were run; every score comes from the rows in usecases-verified.md and the rubric. Abstracts and papers cited there were not re-read, so confidence is capped at medium and mostly low.

DOIs for PMIDs 42662728, 42318218, 42697708, 14693724, 18628574, 32219329, 22963817, 32873586, 23890130, 38895780, 39994886 are not recorded in usecases-verified.md and were not looked up; the identifier rule is not met for them in this report.
Row 45: fasting-based insulin or HOMA is the assumed measure type; the last 59k characters of ADA section 3 were unread.
Row 20: abstract-level and case-series sources; the Cryer 2009 guideline was not read.

Measure types: row 20 and 25 total insulin with C-peptide and PEG precipitation (fasting or spontaneous-hypoglycaemia sample); row 8 and 27 mixed-meal C-peptide; row 11 C-peptide (unspecified fasting or random); row 48 post-load and mixed-meal glucose with insulin.
